title: What is Redux?
overview: Redux is a predictable state management library used to manage and share application state in a centralized way.

example.title: Redux Purpose
example.content:
Components
 ↓
Redux Store
 ↓
Global State Management

title: Why Use Redux?
overview: Redux helps manage complex application states by providing a single source of truth and predictable data flow.

example.title: Problems Redux Solves
example.content:
Without Redux:
Component → Component → Component

With Redux:
Component → Store → Component

title: Redux Core Principles
overview: Redux follows three main principles: single source of truth, state is read-only, and changes are made using pure functions.

example.title: Redux Principles
example.content:
1. Single Store
2. Immutable State
3. Pure Reducers

title: Redux Data Flow
overview: Redux uses a one-way data flow where actions describe changes and reducers update the store state.

example.title: Redux Flow
example.content:
User Action
 ↓
Dispatch Action
 ↓
Reducer
 ↓
Store Updated
 ↓
UI Updated

title: Redux vs Context API
overview: Redux and Context API both manage state, but Redux provides more advanced tools for large and complex applications.

example.title: Comparison
example.content:
Context API:
Small application state

Redux:
Large application state
Debugging tools
Middleware support

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what Redux is, why it is used, its principles, data flow, and comparison with Context API.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Redux manages global state.
✔ Store holds application state.
✔ Actions describe changes.
✔ Reducers update state.
